questions.question: Six years ago, the average age of L and M was 39 years and the average of the present ages of L, M and N is 54 years. What will be the age of N 5 years from now?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Six years ago, the average age of L and M was 39 years. 

the average present age of L, M and N is 54 years. 

**Formula used:**

** {Average of n number} = {A{tiny1}+A{tiny2}+....+A{tiny n}over n} **

**Calculation:**

Let L,M,N lives in present.

so 6 years ago,

=> {Average of L and M}={(L-6)+(M-6)over 2}=39 

=> (L - 6) + (M - 6) = 39 × 2

=> L + M = 78 + 12 

=> L + M = 90 ....(1)

the average of the present ages of L, M and N is 54 years,

=>{Average age of L, M and N}={L+M+Nover 3}= 54 

=> L + M + N = 54 × 3

=> L + M + N = 162 ... (2)

After combining equations (1) & (2)

=> **L + M** + N = 162

=> 90 + N = 162

=> N = 72

Hence, Age of N after 5 years from now is i.e. 72 + 5 = 77

**Hence, '77' is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Gopal went to a bank to withdraw Rs. 4,000. He asked the cashier to give the cash in Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 notes only. Gopal got 50 notes in all. How many Rs. 50 notes did he receive?

Gopal withdraw Rs. 4,000. 

The cashier to give the cash in Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 notes only. 

Gopal got 50 notes in all.

**Solution:**

Let the Number of notes of 50s and 100s are x, and y respectively.

the cash in Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 notes only , so equation formed as

=> 50x + 100y = 4000

=> x+ 2y = 80 .... (1)

Gopal got 50 notes in all, so the equation formed as,

=> x + y = 50....(2)

Subtracting the eq (2) from (1), we got,

=> y = 80 - 50

=> y = 30

now calculate the value of x from eq (2) as,

=> x + 30 = 50

=> x = 20
